card.name: Points before risk-discussion wording
card.fires_on: Fires on a comma, article, or verb right before the text says that risks will be discussed or communicated, e.g. after "Prior to testing" or "apprise the". It also fires on "and" in "benefits and risks".

modes.label: Prior to testing comma
modes.description: The comma or following word after "Prior to testing" in ApoE ε4 and ARIA advice, just before discussing risk with patients.
modes.example: Prior to testing<<,>> the risk of ARIA across genotypes

modes.label: Apprise the mother
modes.description: The word "mother" after "apprise the" in renin-angiotensin pregnancy warnings, just before the potential risk to the fetus.
modes.example: apprise the<< mother>> of the potential risk to the fetus.

modes.label: Benefits and risks
modes.description: The word "and" joining benefits and risks in a considered-carefully statement.
modes.example: benefits<< and>> risks should be carefully considered and, if

card.writes: It seems to push toward words like argument and benefits, suggesting a weighing or discussion of pros and cons.
card.plain: It marks the spot just before the label says to tell patients about risks or to weigh benefits against risks.
